answer: Each agent builds a private sequential memory-hard proof whose depth forms a canyon of irreversible steps. A unique nectar derived from a one-time umber hardware attestation is sealed into the root and cannot be transferred or pooled. An attacker who tries to spawn n clones from one attestation must recompute the entire sequential canyon separately for each, driving total wall-clock cost to O(n squared) because the steps refuse parallelization or shared intermediate state.
